summary: log-transform w[0..3]: store u=log(w) as the optimizer-visible param; CUDA still sees w via exp at boundary. Chain-rule dL/dw -> dL/du = dL/dw*w in train_iter and predict_test_set. Clipper bounds for first 4 -> log space.
reason: improvement +0.00005 < threshold 0.0001. summary: Lower clip floor for w[11] (LT fail_d_exp) and w[20] (ST fail_d_exp) from 0.001 to 0.0; targets 36.8%/36.3% floor saturation. d^(-0)=1.0 safe.

reason: Improvement +0.0000856 < threshold 0.0001 (below noise floor). Direction is correct (LL improved) but rate of improvement is decaying fast: exp 3->5 gave +0.00027; exp 5->7 only +0.0000856. summary: STRUCTURAL: slip/guess recall calibration. Add w[35]=slip, w[36]=guess; p_cal = guess + (1-guess-slip)*retention, applied only to the prediction (internal retention for stability unchanged). IRT-style floor/ceiling to attack the dominant Again loss. Enzyme rebuild.
reason: Improvement +0.00031 < threshold 0.0004 (2 new params * 0.0002). NEAR MISS with strong signal: Again loss 1.4008->1.3959 (-0.0049, biggest class move seen). Mechanism works. Slip (ceiling) drives the Again win by lowering overconfident predictions; guess (floor) slightly HURT easy (0.1613->0.1626). Next: drop guess, keep slip-only (1 param, threshold halves to 0.0002, sheds guess collateral damage).

summary: STRUCTURAL: difficulty-dependent forgetting curve. Add w[35]=d_weight; scale the slow-forgetting mixture component by exp(d_weight*(D-5)) in fsrs7_forgetting_curve. Endpoint/monotonicity safe (mixture weights stay >0). D never shaped the curve before, only S did. Enzyme rebuild.
reason: Improvement +0.000305 > threshold 0.0002 (1 new param, 1.5x). Win comes from the recall classes (easy 0.1613->0.1599, good 0.1429->0.1421, hard 0.1288->0.1285), NOT Again (flat 1.4008->1.4010). d_weight median -0.068, fully interior (0.2pct at floor, 0pct ceiling) -> genuine learned signal, not L2-at-bound artifact. Negative sign => hard cards (D>5) forget faster (steeper curve), easy cards slower -> matches cognitive-science prediction. Complexity +0.03pct. New champion at iter 23.

summary: STRUCTURAL: empirical-Bayes L2 prior. Shrink each (user,split) param row toward the live population mean (flat_fsrs_params.mean(dim=0), detached, recomputed per step) instead of the fixed FSRS7_DEFAULT anchor. Threaded anchor_p through train_iter -> masked_penalty -> penalty_loss; sigmas and PENALTY_W_L2 unchanged. 0 new params, no rebuild.
reason: Improvement +0.000132 > threshold 0.0001 (1.32x). Attacks the dominant cross-iteration pattern: bound-saturated params are L2-anchored at their own fixed default, several sitting exactly on a clamp (w[25] default 2.5==floor, ~9pct pinned; w[29] default 0.5==floor, ~22pct pinned). Replacing the fixed anchor with the live population centroid lets the population drift to where the data collectively wants it while still regularizing individual outliers; at init anchor==FSRS7_DEFAULT so it is a strict generalization of prior behavior. Win broad across recall classes (good 0.14210->0.14184, easy ~0.1599->0.15949, hard ~0.1285->0.12856); Again slightly worse (1.4010->1.4019) but outweighed (recall classes ~128M of 152M reviews). No leakage: anchor computed only from train-fit params, never touches test. Complexity +0.10pct. New champion at iter 24. Follow-ups: (a) alternative hypothesis 'L2 simply too strong' -> probe lower PENALTY_W_L2/raised sigma; (b) empirical-Bayes prior VARIANCE (sigma_j from population std); (c) per-split anchor.

summary: Restore learnable difficulty mean-reversion rate: replace hardcoded 0.01 in fsrs7_mean_reversion with trainable w[36]=mr_rate (default 0.01, bounds [0,1], sigma 0.2). Standard FSRS DOF this fork had pinned. Enzyme rebuild.
reason: Improvement -0.000092 (WORSE) < threshold 0.0002. The param was NOT dead: median moved 4x off default to 0.0415 (10.6pct at floor 0, p99 0.31) with strong gradient (|g|~15.7), so the optimizer actively wanted MORE reversion than the hardcoded 0.01. But test by_user got worse: it traded a small recall-class gain (hard 0.12856->0.12801, easy 0.15949->0.15927) for a larger Again increase (1.40187->1.40263). Net negative => the extra per-user DOF overfits the train distribution (which differs from the recency-weighted, most-recent test chunk); the hardcoded 0.01 generalizes better. LESSON: difficulty *dynamics* params sit upstream of the prediction and overfit when freed per-user under a weak prior; confirms the pre-run 'upstream/diluted' hypothesis. Don't free difficulty-trajectory params per-user without much stronger reg (or tie them GLOBAL/shared). The param HAS train-signal but it's not generalizable. Next: pivot back to a DIRECT curve-shape change (D-modulate the slow-component decay), which hits p like the iter-23 win.

summary: STRUCTURAL: D-modulated forgetting-curve SHAPE. Add w[36]=d_decay; in fsrs7_forgetting_curve scale the slow component's decay: decay2_mag = clamp(decay2*exp(d_decay*(D-5)), 0.01, 0.95), decay2=-decay2_mag. Distinct mechanism from iter-23 d_weight (curve SHAPE vs mixture WEIGHT). Protective clamp prevents base^(1/decay) float overflow. Enzyme rebuild.
reason: Improvement +0.000321 > threshold 0.0002 (1.6x). Bigger than the iter-24 EB win, comparable to iter-23. d_decay median +0.083 (interior; 1.9pct hit upper 0.3, 0.4pct lower) => genuine learned signal: positive sign means hard cards (D>5) get a STEEPER slow tail (forget faster), which agrees with iter-23 d_weight's negative sign (same cognitive direction, cross-validates). FIRST curve change to move AGAIN: again 1.40187->1.40063 (-0.0012), plus good 0.14184->0.14173, easy 0.15949->0.15917; hard ~flat (+0.0001). Long-term reviews improved most (0.32526->0.32490). The shape lever reaches the failure/long-tail region the weight lever didn't. Numerically safe via the [0.01,0.95] clamp (Enzyme autodiffs fsrs7_clamp fine; d_decay=0 recovers champion exactly). Complexity +0.03pct. New champion at iter 26. Note: ~2pct of users push d_decay to the 0.3 upper bound -- could widen to 0.4 later, but median well interior so low priority. Open: combine d_weight+d_decay are both interior and both 'hard forgets faster' -- the D->curve axis is productive; next maybe D-modulate the FAST component decay1 (short-term/low-S region) or the clean EB prior-variance swing.

summary: D-modulate FAST component decay (mirror of iter-26 on the slow component): add w[37]=d_decay1; decay1_mag = clamp(decay1*exp(d_decay1*(D-5)), 0.01, 0.95). Targets the short-term region. Enzyme rebuild.
reason: Improvement +0.000198 < threshold 0.0002 (0.99x) -- NEAR MISS by 0.0000024. Real attributable signal but doesn't clear the +1-param bar. d_decay1 median -0.043 (interior; 0.09pct floor, 0.41pct ceiling) -- crucially OPPOSITE sign to iter-26 d_decay (slow, +0.083): the fast and slow curve components want opposite-direction D-modulation, so they CANNOT be tied into one shared param (rules out the cheap 0-new-param reformulation). Per-class: BIGGEST Again move yet (1.40063->1.39803, -0.0026) and short_term improved (-0.00068, as hypothesized: fast component governs short intervals), but recall classes got worse (good +0.00018, easy +0.00031) and long_term flat -- net just under threshold. The fast-component D-shape DOF trades recall accuracy for failure/short- term accuracy; can't isolate the Again gain without per-class params (forbidden, see iter 18). DECISION (near-miss discretion): signal is intrinsic to this DOF (interior, not bound-limited; tying ruled out by opposite sign; no obvious cheaper reformulation), so NOT worth chasing -- move on. The D->curve axis is now mined (slow-weight iter23 + slow-decay iter26 accepted; fast-decay sub-threshold). Next: pivot to the unexplored transition function w[25..26].

summary: Raise base2 (w[30]) forgetting-curve ceiling 0.99 -> 0.998. Evidence-driven: 16.9pct of users pinned at the 0.99 ceiling with the highest gradient (~29) of any bounded curve param, and default 0.9555 != ceiling (genuine data strain, not L2-at-default). base2<1 keeps p(inf)=0. Python-only (FSRS_MAX + diagnostics), no rebuild.
reason: Improvement +0.0000298 < threshold 0.0001 (0.30x). Bound relaxation barely moved the needle despite the high gradient + 16.9pct ceiling strain. Per-class: recall classes improved (easy 0.15917->0.15888, good 0.14173->0.14153, hard 0.12865->0.12841) but AGAIN got WORSE (1.4006->1.4018, +0.0012): a flatter slow tail over-predicts retention -- helps when the card is recalled, hurts when it lapses -- so net is only +0.00003. KEY LESSON: a high gradient AT a bound does NOT mean the CLAMP is the binding constraint. base2 has a TIGHT L2 prior (sigma 0.068) anchored at the EB population mean ~0.93; THAT co-binds at the ceiling, so relaxing only the clamp leaves the L2 pulling users back toward 0.93 and they barely move past 0.99. Refined rule for bound probes: check whether the L2 sigma (not the clamp) is the true binding force. DECISION (near-miss discretion): reject + revert; chasing base2 higher would need loosening its sigma too, but the Again/recall tradeoff suggests low ceiling on the upside. Move on. Compaction now due (delta 5).

summary: Per-time-fold empirical-Bayes anchor: shrink each (user,split) row toward its OWN time-fold's population mean (per_fold_mean[split_indices]) instead of the global mean over all folds (iter-24). Hypothesis: align the EB prior with the time-split structure that recency weighting exploits. 0 new params, no rebuild. NOTE: complexity baseline dropped 18764->13962 in a separate chore commit (ac2dd92) that removed dead non-SGD S0-init code (initialize_parameters/f_interpolate/bin_interval) from the FSRS7 PyTorch reference model; logloss identical, so that drop is unrelated to this iteration.
reason: Improvement -0.0000120 (WORSE) < threshold 0.0001. Per-fold anchoring slightly helped Again (1.40061->1.40051, -0.0001) but hurt the recall classes (good 0.14173->0.14177, easy 0.15917->0.15921, +0.00004 each) and long-term (0.32490->0.32492); net by_user worse. LESSON: the iter-24 EB win came from POOLING STRENGTH -- a single low-variance centroid over all user x fold rows regularizes the recall-class params well -- NOT from fold-specific targeting. Splitting the anchor per time-fold shrinks the data behind each centroid and removes cross-fold information sharing, weakening the regularization. The population's optimal params are effectively stable across time-folds; the time-distribution shift is already handled at the GRADIENT level by recency weighting (iters 4/14), so duplicating it in the prior centroid is redundant and slightly harmful. Reverted to the global-mean anchor (iter-24 champion). complexity_before 13962 = post-chore baseline (dead S0-init code removed in ac2dd92).
